lead_cast: Marlon Brando, Al Pacino, James Caan
blurb: Puzo co-wrote the screenplay with Coppola, so the film keeps the novel's family saga and its weight while trimming its many subplots. It won Best Picture and remains the benchmark for the crime epic.

lead_cast: Tim Robbins, Morgan Freeman, Bob Gunton
blurb: Darabont adapted a novella from King's 1982 collection Different Seasons, keeping Red's narration nearly intact. A box-office disappointment on release, it found its audience on home video and television and became one of the most beloved films ever made.

lead_cast: Gregory Peck, Mary Badham, Phillip Alford
blurb: Horton Foote's screenplay trims the novel's sprawl but keeps Scout's child's-eye view of Maycomb. Harper Lee was so moved by Gregory Peck's Oscar-winning Atticus Finch that she gave him her father's pocket watch.

lead_cast: Sam Neill, Laura Dern, Jeff Goldblum
blurb: Spielberg kept Crichton's premise but softened the novel's darker edges, sparing characters the book kills off. Its blend of Stan Winston's animatronics and early CG dinosaurs reinvented the summer blockbuster and still holds up.

lead_cast: Jack Nicholson, Shelley Duvall, Danny Lloyd
blurb: Kubrick's cold, geometric vision diverged sharply from King's novel, trading its tragedy of a decent man undone by drink for something more ambiguous. King disliked it enough to make his own miniseries in 1997; audiences and critics sided with Kubrick.

movie_title: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest
lead_cast: Jack Nicholson, Brad Dourif, Louise Fletcher
book_title: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest
blurb: Forman dropped Chief Bromden's narration from Kesey's novel, shifting the centre of gravity to McMurphy; Kesey objected and said he never watched the film. It swept the five major Oscars, only the second film to do so after It Happened One Night.

lead_cast: Edward Norton, Brad Pitt, Helena Bonham Carter
blurb: Fincher kept Palahniuk's premise and much of his dialogue, changing chiefly the ending. Palahniuk has said he thought the film improved on his book, and after a disappointing release it became a cult touchstone on DVD.

lead_cast: Malcolm McDowell, Patrick Magee, Carl Duering
blurb: Kubrick worked from the American edition of Burgess's novel, which omitted the final chapter in which Alex outgrows violence. Burgess spent years distancing himself from the film's bleaker ending and the notoriety it brought him.

lead_cast: Javier Bardem, Tommy Lee Jones, Josh Brolin
blurb: The Coen brothers followed McCarthy's novel almost line for line, preserving its silences and its refusal to romanticize violence. It won four Oscars including Best Picture, and Javier Bardem's Anton Chigurh became one of cinema's most unsettling villains.

lead_cast: Ben Affleck, Rosamund Pike, Neil Patrick Harris
blurb: Flynn wrote the screenplay herself, trimming the plot but keeping the novel's dual-narrator twist and its central cruelty intact. Fincher's cold palette and Rosamund Pike's Oscar-nominated Amy matched the material exactly.

lead_cast: Jodie Foster, Anthony Hopkins, Scott Glenn
blurb: Demme turned Harris's procedural thriller into something closer to a chamber piece, built around close-up conversations. Hopkins's Lecter appears for roughly sixteen minutes yet dominates the film, which became the third to sweep the five major Oscars.

movie_title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
lead_cast: Daniel Craig, Rooney Mara, Christopher Plummer
book_title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
blurb: Hollywood's version arrived two years after the Swedish adaptation, with Steven Zaillian's script reworking how the Harriet Vanger mystery resolves. Rooney Mara took Lisbeth Salander to a quieter, more wounded register than Noomi Rapace's.

movie_title: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
lead_cast: Elijah Wood, Ian McKellen, Viggo Mortensen
blurb: Jackson condensed Tolkien's opening volume, cutting Tom Bombadil and expanding Arwen, without losing the book's weight or its sense of deep history. Shot back to back with its sequels, it began a trilogy that closed with eleven Oscars for The Return of the King.

movie_title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
lead_cast: Daniel Radcliffe, Rupert Grint, Emma Watson
book_title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
blurb: Columbus's faithful first chapter set the visual template the remaining seven films would build on. Rowling insisted on a British cast, and Steve Kloves's script kept nearly every major scene from the book.

lead_cast: Jennifer Lawrence, Josh Hutcherson, Liam Hemsworth
blurb: Collins co-wrote the screenplay, swapping Katniss's first-person narration for scenes with the Gamemakers that the book could never show. Jennifer Lawrence's Katniss carried the franchise and reset what a YA lead could look like on screen.

lead_cast: Timothée Chalamet, Rebecca Ferguson, Oscar Isaac
blurb: Villeneuve adapted only the first half of Herbert's dense novel, giving each sequence room to breathe where David Lynch's 1984 version had tried to compress everything. It won six Oscars and set up a second part that finished the book in 2024.

lead_cast: Harrison Ford, Rutger Hauer, Sean Young
book_title: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
blurb: Scott kept Dick's central question, what makes someone human, and discarded most of his plot, including the electric sheep and the religion of Mercerism. Dick died months before release but saw early footage and approved of what he saw.

lead_cast: Suraj Sharma, Irrfan Khan, Ayush Tandon
blurb: Ang Lee turned a novel long considered unfilmable into a landmark of digital effects, with a CG tiger and ocean that rarely look fake. The frame story keeps Martel's central ambiguity intact, and Lee won Best Director for it.

lead_cast: James McAvoy, Keira Knightley, Saoirse Ronan
blurb: Christopher Hampton's script keeps McEwan's three-part structure, so the final revelation lands as hard on screen as on the page. Joe Wright's five-minute tracking shot across the Dunkirk beach became the film's signature.

lead_cast: Ralph Fiennes, Juliette Binoche, Willem Dafoe
blurb: Minghella reshaped Ondaatje's fragmentary novel into a more linear romance, shrinking Kip's story along the way. Ondaatje collaborated closely on the adaptation, and the film won nine Oscars including Best Picture.

lead_cast: Timothée Chalamet, Armie Hammer, Michael Stuhlbarg
blurb: Guadagnino kept Aciman's languorous Italian summer but ended before the novel's epilogue spanning twenty years. James Ivory's screenplay won an Oscar, and Chalamet's long final close-up became the film's most-discussed moment.

lead_cast: Keira Knightley, Matthew Macfadyen, Brenda Blethyn
blurb: Wright's adaptation chose atmosphere over wit: rain, candlelight, muddy hems and a hand flexing after a single touch. Keira Knightley's Oscar-nominated Elizabeth became the definitive one for a new generation.

lead_cast: Saoirse Ronan, Emma Watson, Florence Pugh
blurb: Gerwig reordered Alcott's chronology, cutting between the sisters' childhood and adulthood, and gave Jo an ending that nods to Alcott's own dealings with her publisher. The film reads as a conversation with the novel rather than a transcription of it.

movie_title: The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
lead_cast: Georgie Henley, Skandar Keynes, William Moseley
book_title: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
blurb: Adamson's adaptation hit every major beat of Lewis's novel and expanded the battle the book only sketches. The Christian allegory survived largely intact, and the film became one of the biggest hits of 2005.

lead_cast: Leonardo DiCaprio, Tobey Maguire, Carey Mulligan
blurb: Luhrmann staged Fitzgerald's novel as spectacle, with a Jay-Z-produced soundtrack under 1920s imagery. Much of the text survives in Nick's voice-over, recast as a memoir he writes from a sanatorium, a frame that isn't in the book.

lead_cast: Gary Oldman, Winona Ryder, Anthony Hopkins
blurb: Despite the title, Coppola added a reincarnated-lover romance that isn't in Stoker. Its in-camera effects, Eiko Ishioka's Oscar-winning costumes and Oldman's performance made it the dominant Dracula of its generation.

lead_cast: Tom Hanks, Audrey Tautou, Ian McKellen
blurb: Howard and screenwriter Akiva Goldsman kept Dan Brown's plot close to the book, puzzles and all. Critics were cool, but the novel's controversy helped make it one of the biggest hits of 2006.

movie_title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
lead_cast: Martin Freeman, Yasiin Bey, Zooey Deschanel
book_title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
blurb: Adams worked on the screenplay for years before his death in 2001, and the film includes new material he wrote for it, such as the character Humma Kavula. Fans of the radio series, books and TV serial were divided; newcomers often found it baffling.

lead_cast: Dev Patel, Freida Pinto, Madhur Mittal
blurb: Simon Beaufoy's script keeps Swarup's quiz-show frame but renames the hero Jamal Malik and turns the novel's picaresque satire into a love story. It won eight Oscars including Best Picture and brought Mumbai's slums to a global audience.

lead_cast: Tom Hanks, Robin Wright, Gary Sinise
blurb: Zemeckis's film sanded off the edges of Groom's bawdy, satirical novel, turning its rougher hero into something sweeter. The book's Forrest goes to space with an orangutan; the film's never leaves the planet, and it won six Oscars including Best Picture.

lead_cast: Brad Pitt, Jonah Hill, Philip Seymour Hoffman
book_title: Moneyball: The Art of Winning an Unfair Game
blurb: Lewis's book introduced sabermetrics to a mass audience. The film, scripted by Steven Zaillian and Aaron Sorkin, kept its central argument of data against baseball orthodoxy and gave it a human face in Billy Beane's 2002 season.

lead_cast: Jesse Eisenberg, Andrew Garfield, Armie Hammer
blurb: Aaron Sorkin adapted Mezrich's book but took it in his own direction, framing Facebook's founding through two lawsuits. Mark Zuckerberg disputed its portrayal; the film won three Oscars, including Sorkin's for the screenplay.

lead_cast: Leonardo DiCaprio, Tom Hanks, Christopher Walken
blurb: Spielberg's lightest film in years, built from Frank Abagnale's memoir of his teenage career as a forger and impostor. Later investigations, notably Alan Logan's 2020 book, have cast serious doubt on how much of it actually happened.

lead_cast: James Franco, Kate Mara, Amber Tamblyn
book_title: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
blurb: Boyle built a feature-length film around a single trapped man, drawing on Ralston's memoir of being pinned by a boulder in a Utah canyon. James Franco carries nearly every scene, and the film earned six Oscar nominations.

lead_cast: Taraji P. Henson, Octavia Spencer, Janelle Monáe
blurb: Shetterly's book recovered the story of the Black women mathematicians whose work at NASA had long been overlooked. The film compressed the timeline and invented some scenes for drama but kept the central injustice in focus.

lead_cast: Russell Crowe, Jennifer Connelly, Ed Harris
blurb: Nasar's biography of John Nash was a detailed, often unflattering portrait. Howard's film kept the arc of his schizophrenia and recovery, made his hallucinations visual, and left out much of his personal life; it won four Oscars including Best Picture.

lead_cast: Aamir Khan, R. Madhavan, Sharman Joshi
blurb: Hirani's film takes the engineering-college setting and three-friend spine from Bhagat's novel but reinvents nearly everything else, which led to a public dispute over credit. It became the highest-grossing Indian film of its time.

lead_cast: Shah Rukh Khan, Aishwarya Rai Bachchan, Madhuri Dixit
blurb: Bhansali's maximalist version arrived after decades of Devdas adaptations, including Bimal Roy's 1955 classic. The sets and costumes run to excess, but the novel's doomed love survives under all the chandeliers.

lead_cast: Dev Anand, Waheeda Rehman, Leela Chitnis
blurb: Vijay Anand's film kept Narayan's story of a tour guide mistaken for a holy man but gave it a more spiritual ending and a celebrated S.D. Burman score. Narayan disliked it enough to write a mocking essay about it; audiences made it a classic.

lead_cast: Urmila Matondkar, Manoj Bajpayee, Sanjay Suri
blurb: Dwivedi adapted Amrita Pritam's Partition novel with care, following a Hindu woman abducted by a Muslim man in the years before the border was drawn. Urmila Matondkar and Manoj Bajpayee anchor a film about the women Partition left behind.

lead_cast: Prosenjit Chatterjee, Tota Roy Chowdhury, Aishwarya Rai Bachchan
blurb: Rituparno Ghosh brought Tagore's novel of desire and widowhood to screen, with Aishwarya Rai as the young widow Binodini. It won the National Film Award for Best Bengali Feature and is faithful enough to work as a companion to the book.

lead_cast: Saif Ali Khan, Vidya Balan, Sanjay Dutt
blurb: Pradeep Sarkar moved Chattopadhyay's 1914 novella to 1960s Calcutta, keeping its romantic core while softening its social critique. Vidya Balan's debut as Lalita won her the Filmfare award for Best Female Debut.

lead_cast: Sushant Singh Rajput, Rajkummar Rao, Amit Sadh
blurb: Kapoor's film adapts Bhagat's novel about three friends in Ahmedabad, with the 2001 Gujarat earthquake and the 2002 riots as its backdrop. It marked Sushant Singh Rajput's film debut and is widely seen as the strongest Bhagat adaptation.

lead_cast: Alia Bhatt, Arjun Kapoor, Amrita Singh
book_title: 2 States: The Story of My Marriage
blurb: Varman's adaptation stays close to Bhagat's semi-autobiographical novel about a Punjabi boy and a Tamil girl who must win over each other's families. The film trades some of the book's sharper humour for warmer rom-com beats.

lead_cast: Rekha, Farooq Shaikh, Naseeruddin Shah
blurb: Muzaffar Ali's adaptation of Ruswa's Urdu novel recreates nineteenth-century Lucknow with rare care, set to Khayyam's ghazals. Rekha's performance as the courtesan won a National Award and has defined the role ever since.

lead_cast: Guru Dutt, Meena Kumari, Waheeda Rehman
blurb: Abrar Alvi directed and Guru Dutt produced this adaptation of Bimal Mitra's novel about a decaying zamindar household in Calcutta. Meena Kumari's Chhoti Bahu, a wife who takes to drink to hold on to her husband, remains one of Hindi cinema's great performances.

lead_cast: Nirmal Pandey, Rajit Kapur, Mohan Agashe
blurb: Pamela Rooks adapted Khushwant Singh's novel of Mano Majra, a Punjabi village where Sikhs and Muslims lived together until a train of corpses arrived. The film keeps the novel's refusal to look away from the violence of Partition.

lead_cast: Priyanka Chopra Jonas, Vivaan Shah, Konkona Sen Sharma
blurb: Vishal Bhardwaj expanded Ruskin Bond's short story into a darkly comic chronicle of one woman's seven marriages. Priyanka Chopra plays Susanna across the decades, and Bond himself appears in a cameo.

lead_cast: Shreya Sharma, Pankaj Kapur, Deepak Dobriyal
blurb: Bhardwaj's gentle adaptation of Ruskin Bond's novella follows a village girl whose umbrella becomes the envy of the Himalayan hills. Pankaj Kapur's miserly shopkeeper carries the moral weight, and the film won the National Award for Best Children's Film.

lead_cast: Kal Penn, Irrfan Khan, Tabu
blurb: Mira Nair's film follows a Bengali family across two generations in America, staying close to Lahiri's novel. Irrfan Khan and Tabu, as the immigrant parents, give it its quiet gravity.

studio: National Film Development Corporation of India
lead_cast: Chandrakant Kulkarni, Chandrakant Mandare, Adhishree Atre
blurb: Amol Palekar adapted Vyankatesh Madgulkar's 1955 novel about a young teacher sent to a shepherd village in drought-stricken Maharashtra. Madgulkar wrote the screenplay himself, and the film won the National Award for Best Marathi Feature.

lead_cast: Arun Sarnaik, Nilu Phule, Shriram Lagoo
blurb: Jabbar Patel's political drama weaves together two Arun Sadhu novels, Simhasan and Mumbai Dinank, in Vijay Tendulkar's scathing script about a power struggle around Maharashtra's chief minister. Its ensemble includes Nilu Phule, Shriram Lagoo and a young Nana Patekar.

lead_cast: Ryan Gosling, Sandra Hüller
blurb: Drew Goddard, who also adapted The Martian, scripted Lord and Miller's take on Weir's novel, dropping the amnesia subplot and revealing Rocky early. The alien was puppeteered rather than CG, and the film opened to strong reviews and $80 million in the US.
